name: Craniorachischisis
aliases: Neural tube defect with anencephaly and contiguous spinal dysraphism

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and imaging diagnosis of craniorachischisis

criteria.description: Presence of anencephaly characterized by absence of the cranial vault and cerebral hemispheres
Contiguous open neural tube defect involving the spinal column (spina bifida aperta)
Failure of neural tube closure extending from the cranial region through the spine

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of both anencephaly and contiguous open spinal neural tube defect confirmed clinically and/or by imaging
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is typically made prenatally by ultrasound or postnatally by clinical examination.

laboratory: Elevated maternal serum alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) during pregnancy
imaging: Prenatal ultrasound showing absent cranial vault and contiguous spinal defect
MRI demonstrating extent of neural tube defect
other: Folic acid deficiency as a significant risk factor

distinguishingFeatures: Absence of cranial vault without contiguous spinal defect
Open spinal defect without associated anencephaly
Herniated brain tissue through skull defect, cranial vault present

redFlags: Absence of cranial vault on prenatal ultrasound
Contiguous open spinal defect visible on imaging
Polyhydramnios in pregnancy indicating impaired fetal swallowing
references: Copp AJ, Stanier P, Greene ND. Neural tube defects: recent advances, unsolved questions, and controversies. Lancet Neurol. 2013 Aug;12(8):799-810.
Greene ND, Copp AJ. Neural tube defects. Annu Rev Neurosci. 2014;37:221-42.
